text: I inherited the farm leadership from my father.
He died during a poor harvest year.
That year people argued more than they worked.
I learned early that blame spreads faster than crops grow.
The terraces were already ancient when I took over.
No one knows who originally built them.
They still work, which is what matters.
The river channels sometimes change slightly after heavy rains.
We repair them every season.
If we don’t, crops fail quickly.
I have seen strange carvings near irrigation stonework upstream.
Bran says the forest hides older paths.
I don’t have time to confirm that.
The temple asks for offerings during harvest festivals.
I don’t object, as long as it doesn’t delay planting.
Nara once said the crops are 'blessed.'
I don’t know what that means in practical terms.
The Night of Ash damaged several storage huts.
After that year, food shortages lasted longer than expected.
People still blame different causes for it.
I blame poor planning and bad weather.
But I don’t say that loudly in temple meetings.
Noki spends too much time listening to Sena’s stories.
I worry he will become distracted from real work.
Mara believes we should store more grain than tradition allows.
She is usually right.
Tarek trusts the system too much.
Systems fail under pressure.
I have seen it before.
The mountain always takes back what people assume is stable.
